text.p: Ato Bolden passed a self-imposed trial with flying colours on Sunday by speeding to world best times in both the 60 and 200 metres at the Birmingham indoor grand prix.
The Olympic 100 and 200 metres bronze medallist equalled Jamaican Michael Green's 60 metres mark of 6.49 before taking to the boards less than an hour later for the 200 metres.
This time the Trinidadian was even more impressive, clocking a season's best of 20.35 seconds ahead of Norway's European outdoor 200 metres gold medallist Geir Moen.

A relieved Boldon said he had needed a good performance here to confirm he would compete in the world indoor championships in Paris next month after finishing last over 60 metres in Lievin, France, last Sunday.
"I can't lose to people indoors who I can beat outdoors," he said. "My start has gone on vacation for the past two weeks.
"I thought maybe I was an outdoor guy. Today was a pleasant surprise."

Then, with his self-confidence evidently returning by the minute, Boldon said he planned to upstage the 150 metres showdown between Olympic 200 metres champion Michael Johnson and Atlanta 100 gold medallist Donovan Bailey in Toronto on May 31.
Boldon said he would attempt the world 100 metres record next month, adding: "I'm going to throw a monkey wrench in the works."
Jamaica's roving ambassador Merlene Ottey, now 36 but showing no signs of slowing down, finished second in the women's 60 metres and confirmed she would be defending her title in Paris.
"I've been talking about retiring since 1984," she said. "I think it's best I shut up now."

Kenya's world 3,000 metres steeplechase record holder Moses Kiptanui ran away with the 3,000 metres in seven minutes 36.78 seconds then looked forward confidently to meeting Ethiopian world record holder Haile Gebreselassie in Paris.
Kiptanui predicted a tactical race at the world championships, although acknowledging the danger of running too slowly over the early laps.
"If it's going to be slow then we have a lot of sprinters behind us, if it's too slow then I might even lose it," he said.
Britain's latest 400 metres hope Jamie Baulch ended the track events in style by defeating American world indoor champion Darnell Hall for the fourth time in succession this season.
Then, as a bonus for those spectators remaining in the arena, Steve Smith, the Olympic bronze medallist, set a year's best in the high jump with a leap of 2.34 metres.

In effort to make the meeting attractive to a younger audience, promoters played throbbing rock music throughout the competition and a track announcer gave a continuous commentary over the public address system as well as enjoining the crowd to make plenty of noise.

The music, though, probably reflected the age of the organisers rather than the youngsters they hoped to attract with the soundtrack dominated by 1960s groups including the Rolling Stones and the Spencer Davis group.
